scope: Primary-source context; not reproduced results or the provenance of our authored8 tasks

papers.title: From Prompts to Posteriors: Can LLM Agents Perform Bayesian Inference in Context?
papers.abstract_level_finding: The authors evaluate probabilistic coherence, quantitative updating and downstream effects. They report frequent Bayesian violations without tools, with substantially improved posterior approximation when reasoning and code execution are available.
papers.local_boundary: Our restricted-network/exact-solver study is much narrower and fictional. It is NOT a replication, does not execute model code, and has no result yet. A tool solver cannot repair incorrect problem extraction automatically.

papers.title: BayesBench: Evaluating LLM Belief Trajectories Under Multi-Turn Evidence Accumulation
papers.abstract_level_finding: Three sequential simulation settings distinguish latent estimation, prediction and persona-framed prediction. The authors report that improved latent inference does not necessarily transfer to accurate outcome predictions.
papers.local_boundary: Single-turn posterior arithmetic is insufficient to establish sequential belief updating or using uncertainty to make good decisions. Do not confuse this paper with other unrelated projects also named BayesBench.

interpretation: Exact solver parity is infrastructure, faithful text-to-network extraction is a separate empirical hurdle, and reliable downstream action is another. None alone establishes broad intelligence, clinical/legal/tax reliability or calibrated uncertainty.
